Robin Hale.narrative: I am eleven and I have been coughing since the spring, so I lie by the fire most days and watch the smoke go up the chimney. I want to go out with Uncle Ned and see the road, but Mother looks at me strangely when I ask. The house is always full of people and talk, and I know the woods around Coldwell better than I know anything else.
values: the fire and the warm corner
goals: to stop coughing and be let out of the house
to go with Uncle Ned on the road one day
to see what is past the trees at the field edge
to stop coughing so he can go outside again
to learn one new thing about the woods each day and keep it

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She sits by me when the coughing is bad and her hands are cold; I wish she would not look at me like that.

relations.name: Aldwin Hale
relations.label: grandfather
relations.note: He tells me about the garden before the Lean Year and lets me hold the seed basket.

relations.name: Ned Hale
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: He says he will take me out when I am strong, and he always smells of the road.

relations.name: Sayer Hale
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She keeps the pot going and puts the warmest bit in my bowl.

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: the sister who nursed me
relations.note: I remember her hands and a bitter drink last winter; Mother speaks well of her.

relations.name: Kai Ostrander
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: He is quiet and watches the road, and he showed me how to hold a stick like a sword.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She used to bring honey cakes when she visited Coldwell before, and Mother says she is my aunt and works at the inn in the town, but I have not seen her since the fever and I wonder if she would still know me.

memories.gist: The winter I had the fever, and a sister in grey came out from the town and sat with me three nights.
Before the Lean Year, running the field boundary with the dog while the men cut the last of the grain.
The day the town men came and said the fields were the store's now, and Mother stood in the door and would not move.
Lying by the fire this spring, hearing Uncle Ned and Hob Ferrier talk about the carts on the road and what they would do.

stances.why: When I am ill the fire is the only warm thing, and everyone gathers round it.
He is always out and always comes back with something.

pastimes: watching the smoke curl up the chimney and naming the shapes it makes
learning the paths and landmarks of the woods from the doorway and from what Uncle Ned tells him
playing knucklebones by the fire with anyone who sits with him
Robin Hale.calling: I want to walk the road with Uncle Ned and know every tree between here and the gate.

Marta Hale.narrative: I am Marta Hale and these are my fields, whatever the town ledger says. When the blight came we borrowed grain like everyone, and when we could not pay the Reeve took the land and set the Tolleys on it, and then called us outlaws for staying in our own houses. So we stay, and we take a share from the carriers on the stone road, and I hold this house together with what my brother and the others bring in. My son is coughing and thin and I would beg at the gate for him, but I will not be seen doing it.
values: not being made a beggar at the gate
goals: to get the fields back, or a pardon, or enough to live on
to keep Ned from doing something that brings the guards down on us
to see the Tolleys off my land without harming them
to see the Tolleys off her land without harming them

relations.name: Robin Hale
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is all I have left of his father, and the cough will not let go of him.

relations.name: Ned Hale
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He does the hard things for us and I am grateful, but he wants to meet the next cart with more men and I have not said yes.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: younger sister
relations.note: She brings what she can by the south gate; I do not ask her to risk more and I tell no one where it comes from.

relations.name: Aldwin Hale
relations.label: father-in-law
relations.note: He works the old garden patch and will not speak of the Tolleys, which suits me.

relations.name: Sayer Hale
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She keeps the common pot and has been leaving food at a woodpile in Ferncross; I have guessed and said nothing.

relations.name: Kai Ostrander
relations.label: one of mine
relations.note: A quay guard who ran from the Surge and fights better than any of us; I do not ask what he ran from.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: one of mine
relations.note: A boy who came off the works with nothing; I have taken him in as my own and I do not press him about where he came from.

relations.name: Hob Ferrier
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He keeps us in meat and knows the woods, but he and Ned have been walking the field edge and I have told them to stay off it.

relations.name: Hal Tolley
relations.label: the tenant on my land
relations.note: He farms my fields for the Guild and has asked Mercy Abbot for stone to build a wall round the yard, and the Guild has sent none.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: Guild head
relations.note: She holds the lease of my fields and put her tenants on them, and she smiles and talks of trade.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: the Reeve who outlawed us
relations.note: He took the land for the store and set the gate against us; I will not forget it.

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: the sister who nursed Robin
relations.note: She came out to Coldwell in winter when no one else would, and I have sent word through Sayer asking her for medicine again.

relations.name: Bram Fenner
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: Agnes's boy, and he has his mother's face; I would not have him know what his father's gate does to us.

relations.name: Marta Tolley
relations.label: tenant's wife
relations.note: She keeps my house and works my soil and fears me for it, and I cannot say she is wrong to.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He pays the due and curses it, and he carries stone past our door; Ned has taken his loads twice and he comes armed now.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: He is my sister's husband and he takes the due at the south gate in the Reeve's name; I am civil to him for Agnes's sake and no more.

memories.gist: The Lean Year, borrowing grain from the town store against the next harvest like everyone in the north.
The day the Reeve's men read out that our fields were the store's, and the Tolleys came to look at them.
Being declared outlaw at the gate, and coming home to Coldwell and deciding we would not go.
Sister Elspeth sitting three nights with Robin through the fever last winter, and leaving herbs and a prayer.
The second time Ned and the others took a share from a carrier on the stone road by force, and the fear afterwards that the guards would come.
Walking the field boundary where the Tolleys could see me, and saying nothing.

stances.why: We were not paid for them and we will not be starved off them.
Harming the Tolleys would lose us any hope of a pardon, so I have told Ned and Hob to stay off the fields.
What the carriers give keeps the house fed, but a hard robbery will bring the guards down on us all.
She came out to us in winter when no one else in the town would.
I will ask for my son through others, but I will not stand at the gate with my hand out.

pastimes: mending and turning clothes by the fire late into the evening
walking the field edges at first light to see what the ground is doing
sitting with Aldwin while he sorts seed and letting him talk
Marta Hale.calling: I hold this house and this ground together, and I would do the same work in peace if they let me.

Aldwin Hale.narrative: I am seventy and I have farmed this ground since before the town kept a ledger of it. My son is dead and his wife Marta holds the house now, and I do not quarrel with how she holds it; I work the old garden patch behind the house and keep the seed and the baskets. I remember the Lean Year and I will not speak of the Tolleys, and I do not say the Reeve's name in this house if I can help it. The boy is the future of the name and I mean to see him grow.
values: the name of Hale on this ground
goals: to keep the garden patch yielding
to live to see the fields ours again, or at least the house kept
to keep the garden patch yielding through the year

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She holds the house better than my son would have; I keep out of her way and work the garden.

relations.name: Robin Hale
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He is the last of the name and he is too thin; I let him hold the seed basket and tell him the old stories.

relations.name: Ned Hale
relations.label: son-in-law's brother
relations.note: Marta's brother does the hard things and I do not like the talk of carts on the road.

relations.name: Sayer Hale
relations.label: Ned's wife
relations.note: She keeps the pot and is kind enough, though she is not of this house by blood.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: the Reeve
relations.note: He took the fields for the store and called us outlaws for staying in our houses; I will not say his name in this house.

relations.name: Hal Tolley
relations.label: the tenant
relations.note: He walks my son's furrows; I will not speak of him.

relations.name: Hob Ferrier
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He hunted for this steading before the Lean Year and still brings meat, but he is too fond of the road.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: daughter-in-law's sister
relations.note: She married a gate guard, but she is still Coldwell at heart and brings what she can.

memories.gist: Farming this ground with my son before the Lean Year, and the barn full at harvest.
The Lean Year, and borrowing grain from the town store like the rest of the north.
The day the Reeve's men read the fields forfeit and the Tolleys came to look them over.
My son's burial, and Marta standing at the grave with the boy in her arms.
Working the old garden patch this spring, setting seed and mending baskets, because a man must do something.

stances.why: The patch behind the house still feeds us and a man must keep doing something.
Hale blood has farmed here since before the ledger, and I will not be the one to leave.
I remember the Lean Year and I will not speak of the Tolleys or the Reeve to anyone.
Robin is the last of the name and he is too thin; everything else can wait.

pastimes: working the old garden patch behind the house, seed and baskets
sitting on the bench at dusk watching the light go off the field
telling Robin the old names of the fields and where the boundaries ran
Aldwin Hale.calling: I have farmed this ground since before the town kept a ledger of it, and I mean to keep the seed in it.
